name: Ascension protocol / routine posts

card.summary: Forum posts in which a member lays out their full regimen, covering skin, gym, diet and supplements, and tracks before and after photos to show how their look changes.
card.note: Some posted protocols include prescription or research compounds; posts are personal plans, not tested programmes.

quick.overview:
An ascension protocol post is a member's written plan for improving their looks, listing everything they intend to do. Typical headings include heightmaxxing, fat loss, supplements, skincare, training and sometimes surgery.

The point is accountability and feedback: members post the plan, ask others to rate or audit it, and often promise before and after photos.
quick.how: A poster states age, height and goals, lists their diet, exercise, skincare and supplement plan, and invites critique. Followers reply with suggestions or criticism. Some posts are simple lifestyle routines such as steps per day and diet; others include hormones, drugs or planned surgeries.
quick.risks: Posts are personal plans, not clinically tested programmes. Some contain prescription and research compounds taken by teenagers, which medical guidance generally advises against without supervision. Replies from other members are often critical.

lead: Ascension protocols and routines are a posting format on looksmax.org in which members list the full set of changes they plan to make to their appearance, often with a promise to post before and after photos.[1][2] The word ascension refers to improving one's looks.

Content varies widely. One post, from a self-described 17-year-old, lists a stack of compounds and says it will run for four months and asks readers to rate it.[1] Another, from a 17-year-old at 5'7, covers heightmaxxing, fat loss with a meat and fruit based diet, 10,000 daily steps and supplements.[2] A third asks others to audit a plan that includes surgery, gear and softmaxxing.[3]
Replies range from advice to blunt criticism; in one thread a reader says a plan's post-cycle approach shows no research.[3] No studies have examined these protocols as a practice.

angle.text: The post is a planning and accountability tool. Whatever improvement occurs comes from the routines listed in it, such as skincare, training and diet.

infobox: Diet, training, skincare, supplements, sometimes surgery
Before/after photos, requests to rate or audit

paras: A typical post gives age, height, weight and a list of tactics by category. Titles such as rate my ascension routine, ascension protocol will post before and afters, and requests for others to audit a plan illustrate the format.[1][2][3][4]

One poster lists a regimen of hormones, a fat burner, oral isotretinoin and peptides and says he will run it for four months, deciding on further steps from results.[1] Another outlines a primal-style diet, vitamin D and K2, magnesium and collagen, along with the aim of reaching 5'9.[2] A third plans several surgeries including spine surgery, rhinoplasty and canthoplasty abroad, alongside recovery-focused compounds.[3]

Replies include criticism of effort, such as a user saying the plan was a lot of work to avoid doing something simpler, and technical critique of post-cycle plans.[2][3] The more ambitious posts draw the most scrutiny.

lore.intro: Ascension protocol posts are a recurring thread type on looksmax.org.[1][2][3]

claims.claim: A stacked, detailed protocol can raise looks and height in months
claims.believers: Posters describe multi-compound or multi-surgery plans and expect measurable change within a set number of months.[1][3]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested such combined protocols.
